Subject: Post-call recap: TCO & next steps - Zenith AI

Alex / Jordan - thanks again for the 30-minute discovery today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps. I've attached a short TCO workbook and a one-page batching/caching cheatsheet for the pilot.

Key pain points you raised:
- Token spend variance month-over-month with peaks during product launches (current average ~50M tokens/mo, peaks to ~80M).
- Latency-sensitive user flows (P99 target <250ms) for synchronous conversational features.
- Tight budget for Q2: target platform spend <= $25k/month.

Goals we discussed:
- Reduce per-token spend while preserving quality (aim: ~35-50% cost reduction relative to current baseline).
- Keep P99 latency within target under expected peak load.
- Run a 4-6 week pilot to validate savings and quality before committing to reserved capacity.

TCO levers & preliminary modeling (high level):
- Model selection: use a lower-cost, Redwood-verified model variant for high-throughput endpoints (model swap can reduce per-token compute by ~20-30% depending on prompt size).
- Quantization: int8 / mixed-precision option for non-critical endpoints (~10-20% cost reduction with negligible quality delta on many workloads).
- Batching & inference concurrency: continuous batching with a target batch window of 20-40ms for API traffic can lower per-token GPU overhead by ~15-25% at your peak QPS.
- KV/prefix caching: cache repeated prompts and persona/context tokens (we commonly see 10-30% token reduction on assistant-style workloads).
- Routing & fallbacks: route non-critical traffic to cheaper model variants during bursts to stay under budget without impacting core flows.

Example baseline vs. Redwood pilot estimate (rough, for discussion):
- Current baseline (your estimate): 50M tokens/month => ~$20,000/month (you mentioned current vendor avg cost ~0.0004/token).
- Redwood pilot (combined levers): 50M tokens/month => ~$12,500/month (~0.00025/token) => estimated monthly savings ~$7,500 (37.5%).
- If we shave cache/hit-rate improvements and batching at peak, we can push effective cost lower; committed Reserved Dedicated pricing can go further in large commits.

Asks / next steps:
1) Please review the attached TCO workbook; confirm the 50M tokens/month baseline and any seasonal multipliers you expect.
2) Grant a short logs sample (anonymized) or traffic snapshot for Rishi to run more accurate batching/caching modeling (we'll sign an NDA / limited data scope if needed).
3) Schedule a 45-minute technical deep dive next week (Rishi + Priyom) to walk through batching parameters and pilot setup.

Suggested times (PST): Mon 3/9 10am, Tue 3/10 11am, Wed 3/11 2pm - let me know what works.

Thanks again - excited to help you hit the cost and latency targets.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Alex - got it. I've updated the workbook (attached) with a per-10k-token delta table and three cache-hit scenarios (0%, 10%, 20%). High-level numbers included in the sheet, but summary here:

Per-10k-token delta (rough):
- Baseline vendor: ~$3.80 per 10k tokens
- Redwood pilot (no cache): ~$2.50 per 10k tokens
- Redwood pilot (10% cache): ~$2.25 per 10k tokens
- Redwood pilot (20% cache): ~$2.00 per 10k tokens

Sensitivity & notes:
- These are conservative estimates assuming average prompt length ~150 tokens and a mix of chat/gen workloads.
- Batching assumptions: target 25ms batch window at your typical QPS -> modeled 18% GPU cost reduction vs single-request execution. If your traffic pattern has many short-lived single-user requests, the effective benefit moves down - Rishi will model using your sample.
- Pilot scope to prove workload-specific cache hit-rate: we recommend a 4-week test on a representative route (10-20% of traffic) to validate hit rates and quality. Pilot runner estimate: ~$1,200- $2,500 depending on peak volume during the test window (we'll provide a more precise quote once we see the sample).

SOC2 / residency: we are SOC2 Type II compliant; I attached the SOC2 readiness info and can initiate an EU-region pilot if you prefer.

Next: confirm Tue 3/10 11am PT for a technical deep dive - Rishi will prepare the per-10k-token sensitivity table and a recommended pilot config. Also please upload a one-week anonymized traffic sample (or allow us to grab a limited API log extract) so we can model batching properly.

I'll put the invite on the calendar for Tue 3/10 11am PT.

Best,
Marissa
